description: A budget line with `spent` = 0 means nothing has been spent yet, so it is left out of the rate averages.

a.request: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), work out for each event its average spending rate, `spent` ÷ `amount`, across its lines, leaving out lines where `spent` is 0. Then, for each event `type`, average those event-level rates. Return the type, its average spending rate, and that rate divided by the simple mean of the per-type average rates. Ignore missing values in the averages, and don't round.
a.sql:
WITH line_rates AS (
  SELECT b.link_to_event, b.spent * 1.0 / NULLIF(b.amount, 0) AS rate
  FROM budget b
  INNER JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event
  WHERE b.spent IS NOT NULL AND b.spent <> 0 AND b.amount IS NOT NULL
),
event_rates AS (
  SELECT e.event_id, e.type, AVG(lr.rate) AS event_rate
  FROM event e
  JOIN line_rates lr ON lr.link_to_event = e.event_id
  GROUP BY e.event_id, e.type
),
type_rates AS (
  SELECT type, AVG(event_rate) AS avg_rate
  FROM event_rates
  GROUP BY type
)
SELECT type, avg_rate, avg_rate / AVG(avg_rate) OVER () AS relative_rate
FROM type_rates;

b.request: For each event, average `spent` ÷ `amount` over only the budget lines with `spent` > 0 (lines with `spent` = 0 excluded), joining budget to event on `link_to_event` = `event_id` (dropping unmatched lines), then average those event-level rates per `event.type`, and report each type's average rate alongside that rate divided by the unweighted mean of the per-type average rates, without rounding and ignoring NULLs
b.sql: WITH event_rate AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.type, AVG(b.spent * 1.0 / b.amount) AS event_rate FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.spent > 0 AND b.amount <> 0 AND e.type IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.event_id, e.type), type_rate AS (SELECT type, AVG(event_rate) AS avg_rate FROM event_rate GROUP BY type) SELECT type, avg_rate, avg_rate / (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) FROM type_rate) AS rate_vs_mean_type_rate FROM type_rate;

c.request: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), work out for each event its average spending rate, `spent` ÷ `amount`, across its lines. Then, for each event `type`, average those event-level rates. Show the type, its average spending rate, and that rate divided by the simple mean of the per-type average rates. Ignore missing values in the averages, and don't round. A budget line with `spent` = 0 means nothing has been spent yet, so it is left out of the rate averages.
c.sql: WITH line_rates AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.type, b.spent * 1.0 / b.amount AS rate FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.spent IS NOT NULL AND b.spent <> 0 AND b.amount IS NOT NULL AND b.amount <> 0), event_rates AS (SELECT event_id, type, AVG(rate) AS event_rate FROM line_rates GROUP BY event_id, type), type_rates AS (SELECT type, AVG(event_rate) AS type_rate FROM event_rates GROUP BY type) SELECT type, type_rate, type_rate / (SELECT AVG(type_rate) FROM type_rates) AS rate_vs_mean_type_rate FROM type_rates;

d.request:
Rewritten as a standalone question:

For each event, average the rate `spent` ÷ `amount` across its budget lines, using only lines matched to an event (drop unmatched lines). Exclude any line where `spent` = 0, since nothing has been spent yet, so it does not count toward the rate averages. Then, for each event `type`, average those event-level rates. Ignore missing values in all averages and do not round. Show each type, its average spending rate, and that rate divided by the simple mean of the per-type average rates.
d.sql: WITH line_rates AS (SELECT b.link_to_event AS event_id, CAST(b.spent AS REAL) / NULLIF(b.amount, 0) AS rate FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.spent IS NOT NULL AND b.spent <> 0 AND b.amount IS NOT NULL), event_rates AS (SELECT event_id, AVG(rate) AS event_rate FROM line_rates WHERE rate IS NOT NULL GROUP BY event_id), type_rates AS (SELECT e.type AS type, AVG(er.event_rate) AS avg_rate FROM event_rates er JOIN event e ON e.event_id = er.event_id WHERE e.type IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.type) SELECT type, avg_rate, avg_rate / (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) FROM type_rates) AS rate_ratio FROM type_rates ORDER BY type;
